who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), port lane L9b (build side and the old engine's deletion), port-memo-1113
where: crates/blaze-lower (lower_writes, refresh, relower), crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve (unit.rs, job.rs, front_carry.rs); docs/v2/plan/design/front-end-on-memo.md section C
what: The driver lane (blaze-lower makes the snapshot's inputs, blaze-cargo keeps the memo between requests) was started at the same time as L1, which owns base-db's inputs and how a snapshot is built. Every call the driver makes into base-db to create a crate, a source root or a file (`Crate::create`, `Files::set_view_root_from_tree`, `add_crates`, the singletons) had to be written against a guessed signature, and the arena each input lives in (a file shared by a lib and a bin of one package, say) is base-db's decision, not the driver's.
cost: every base-db call in blaze-lower and blaze-cargo written twice: once against an assumed API, again when L1's lands; a list of assumptions the main agent must reconcile
cause: the spec fixes blaze-memo's and hir-def's interfaces for the lanes (sections A and C, 'L1 API' and 'L3 API' to be written) but not base-db's input-making API, which is the driver's whole interface
class: a fan-out whose shared interface is named in the spec only for some of the seams, so the lanes on an unnamed seam guess
prevention: a spec for a fan-out names every cross-lane signature a lane calls (here: how the driver makes each base-db input in which arena), and a lane whose only interface is unnamed waits on it or is merged with its owner
workaround: the lane wrote against the smallest change (same functions, `&Inputs` and a fact in place of `&mut Db` and a durability) and listed each assumption in its report
